operationContexts.label: General solvent pretreatment
operationContexts.description: Before use, solvents were dried over molecular sieves and purged with high-purity Ar for 30 min. This general solvent pretreatment is separate from reaction-mixture room-temperature degassing/N2 backfill and from the separate three-cycle S/OLA sulfur-stock degas.

source_locator.locator: Main PDF p. 2 (printed p. 2892), Materials paragraph

operationContexts.label: Prepare metal precursor mixture
operationContexts.description: General method: reagents in OLA; degas at room temperature, then backfill with nitrogen. For 3:1 rows, absolute feed quantities are unresolved/conflicted except for the 190 °C S/OLA passage.

operationContexts.label: Prepare sulfur source
operationContexts.description: Selected sulfur-source branch: a mixture of 1-dodecanethiol and tert-dodecanethiol in oleylamine. Component amounts/ratio, concentration, stock-preparation details and injection volume are not reported. Elemental S/OLA is a separate, mutually exclusive Figure 1 condition and is not included in this candidate.

operationContexts.label: Hot-injection synthesis
operationContexts.description: Rapidly inject the selected mixed-thiol/oleylamine sulfur source into the heated reaction mixture and stir. Figure 1 gives the temperature-specific outcome; cell-specific dwell and several exact feed amounts remain unknown.

source_locator.locator: main PDF p. 3 (printed p. 2893), Figure 1 and caption
main PDF p. 3 (printed p. 2893), Scheme 1 and Results

operationContexts.label: Precipitation and wash
operationContexts.description: Cool, add hexane and ethanol, centrifuge, isolate black precipitate, and wash three times. Further wash volume/centrifugation details, yield and drying/storage are absent. The paper says the black precipitate was isolated; the retained fraction is not explicitly called a pellet.

general_background.title: Injection and precursor supply
general_background.summary: Rapid injection can concentrate precursor conversion near the start of a reaction, helping distinguish nucleation from subsequent growth. A short period of rapid precursor conversion can favour nucleation, while a later lower supply can favour growth on existing particles.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Destabilizing a particle dispersion
general_background.summary: An antisolvent can solvate a particle's ligand shell less favourably than the original dispersion medium. Reduced solvation can weaken colloidal stability and allow particles to aggregate and separate from the liquid, depending on the ligands and solvent mixture.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Prospects of Colloidal Nanocrystals for Electronic and Optoelectronic Applications
